title: Technical MCQ Set 07: Concurrency Locks, Disk Scheduling & SQL CASE
description: Covers synchronized class vs instance locks, BigDecimal equals vs compareTo, Collectors.toMap trap, SCAN disk scheduling, OSPF/BGP, and JDBC pools.

questions.question: What does the following Java code print?
questions.explanation: `BigDecimal.equals()` compares BOTH numeric value AND scale (`1.0` scale 1 != `1.00` scale 2 => `false`). `BigDecimal.compareTo()` compares numeric value ignoring scale (`0` => `true`).

questions.question: What happens when the following Java code executes?
options: Throws `NullPointerException` on `int y = true ? x : 0;` due to unboxing `x`
questions.explanation: In `true ? x : 0`, one branch is `Integer` and the other is primitive `int`, so Java unboxes `x` (`x.intValue()`) even though the branch evaluates to `x` directly, throwing `NullPointerException`!

questions.question: What happens when executing `Stream.of("apple", "apricot").collect(Collectors.toMap(s -> s.charAt(0), s -> s))`?
questions.explanation: The 2-argument `Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)` throws `IllegalStateException` on duplicate keys unless you pass a 3rd merge-function argument like `(v1, v2) -> v2`.

questions.question: Class `Counter` has `synchronized void incInstance()` and `static synchronized void incStatic()`. If Thread T1 enters `obj.incInstance()` while Thread T2 calls `Counter.incStatic()`, do they block each other?
options: Yes, both acquire the same global JVM lock
No, `incInstance()` locks on `obj` (`this` instance monitor), whereas `incStatic()` locks on `Counter.class` monitor
questions.explanation: Instance synchronized methods acquire the object instance lock (`this`), whereas static synchronized methods acquire the `Class` object lock (`Counter.class`); they are completely independent monitors.

questions.question: How does Java's `ForkJoinPool` keep worker threads balanced during uneven divide-and-conquer tasks?
options: By moving all tasks onto a single main thread
Via work-stealing: idle worker threads steal tasks from the tail of busy workers' double-ended queues (deques)
By locking a single global priority queue on every task push/pop
By spawning an unbounded OS thread per subtask
questions.explanation: Each worker pushes/pops its own subtasks LIFO at the head of its deque (cache-friendly), while idle threads steal older subtasks FIFO from the tail of busy workers' deques.

questions.question: Why can an `abstract class` in Java define constructors even though it cannot be instantiated directly with `new`?
options: To initialize the abstract class's own fields and invariants when invoked via `super(...)` from a concrete subclass constructor
To allow static methods to create instances silently
Java forbids constructors inside abstract classes
questions.explanation: Concrete subclasses invoke `super(...)` during construction, allowing the abstract base class to initialize shared fields cleanly.

questions.question: Table `Txns(dept, status, amount)` has `status` in `('PAID', 'FAILED')`. Which query outputs one row per `dept` with separate `paid_total` and `failed_total` columns?
options: `SELECT dept, SUM(amount) WHERE status='PAID', SUM(amount) WHERE status='FAILED' FROM Txns GROUP BY dept`
`SELECT dept, SUM(CASE WHEN status='PAID' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS paid_total, SUM(CASE WHEN status='FAILED' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS failed_total FROM Txns GROUP BY dept`
`SELECT dept, SUM(amount) FROM Txns GROUP BY dept, status`
questions.explanation: Conditional aggregation (`SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN amount ELSE 0 END)`) pivots status categories into side-by-side columns in one table scan.

questions.question: Which query finds employees in `Emp` whose salary is strictly greater than EVERY salary in department 20 (assuming no NULL salaries)?
options: `SELECT name FROM Emp WHERE salary > ANY (SELECT salary FROM Emp WHERE dept_id = 20)`
`SELECT name FROM Emp WHERE salary > ALL (SELECT salary FROM Emp WHERE dept_id = 20)`
`SELECT name FROM Emp WHERE salary IN (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Emp WHERE dept_id = 20)`
`SELECT name FROM Emp WHERE salary <> ALL (SELECT salary FROM Emp WHERE dept_id = 20)`
questions.explanation: `> ALL (...)` requires the salary to exceed every returned value (equivalent to `> MAX(salary)` when non-empty and non-null), whereas `> ANY (...)` only requires exceeding the minimum.

questions.question: In the ARIES database crash recovery algorithm, what is the correct sequence of its three recovery passes?
questions.explanation: ARIES runs: (1) Analysis (scans forward from last checkpoint to identify dirty pages & active loser transactions), (2) Redo (repeats history from smallest RecLSN), and (3) Undo (rolls back uncommitted loser transactions backward).

questions.question: When joining two large unsorted tables on an equality condition (`a.key = b.key`) without usable indexes, which physical join algorithm typically delivers the best performance when one table's hash table fits in memory?
options: Hash Join (build hash table on smaller relation, probe with larger)
questions.explanation: Hash Join hashes the smaller build input in `O(M)` and streams the probe input in `O(N)`, avoiding the `O(N*M)` nested scan and `O(N log N)` sorting of Sort-Merge.

questions.question: A disk head starts at cylinder `50` with pending requests `{82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190}`. What is the total head movement (in cylinders) using Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF)?
questions.explanation: From 50, closest is 43 (7), then 24 (19), then 16 (8), then from 16 jump to 82 (66), then 140 (58), then 170 (30), then 190 (20). Total = 7 + 19 + 8 + 66 + 58 + 30 + 20 = 208 cylinders (equivalently (50 - 16) + (190 - 16) = 34 + 174 = 208).

questions.question: Why does a 64-bit OS sometimes use an Inverted Page Table (one entry per physical frame) instead of per-process hierarchical page tables?
options: To bound page table memory strictly to physical RAM size rather than scaling with virtual address space * process count
To allow processes to bypass virtual-to-physical translation
To store file directories inside CPU L1 cache
questions.explanation: An inverted page table maintains a single global table with one entry per physical page frame (hashed by `<PID, VPN>`), keeping page table overhead proportional to installed physical RAM.

questions.subtopic: Routing Protocols (RIP vs OSPF vs BGP)
questions.question: Which pairing of routing protocol and underlying algorithm/scope is CORRECT?
options: OSPF -> Intra-AS Link-State (Dijkstra); BGP -> Inter-AS Path-Vector
BGP -> Intra-AS Distance-Vector using hop count max 15
questions.explanation: RIP is intra-AS distance-vector (Bellman-Ford, max 15 hops); OSPF is intra-AS link-state (Dijkstra SPF); BGP is the internet's inter-AS path-vector protocol.

questions.question: What are the minimum fixed header sizes of a standard UDP header and a standard TCP header (without options) respectively?
questions.explanation: A UDP header is 8 bytes (Src Port, Dst Port, Length, Checksum = 4 * 2B). A standard TCP header without options is 20 bytes.

questions.question: In a Red-Black Tree containing `N` internal nodes, what is the guaranteed upper bound on the height of the tree (number of edges on the longest root-to-NIL path)?
questions.explanation: Because no two consecutive red nodes appear on a path and every path has equal black-height `bh >= h/2`, a Red-Black Tree satisfies `h <= 2 * log2(N + 1)`, guaranteeing `O(log N)` operations.

questions.question: After running the Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path algorithm on graph `G`, how do you detect whether `G` contains a negative-weight cycle?
options: Check if any `dist[i][j]` is negative for `i != j`
Check if the graph is disconnected
questions.explanation: Initially `dist[i][i] = 0`. If a vertex `i` can reach itself along a negative total-weight cycle, `dist[i][i]` becomes `< 0`.

questions.question: In a Spring Boot app using HikariCP (default pool size 10), why does forgetting to close a manual `Connection` obtained from `dataSource.getConnection()` quickly freeze the entire application?
options: JDBC closes the JVM after 10 queries
After 10 unclosed borrows, the pool is exhausted and all subsequent threads block until `connectionTimeout` then throw `SQLTransientConnectionException`
HikariCP drops all database tables upon leak detection
questions.explanation: Connections borrowed from a pool must be closed (`try-with-resources`) to return them to the pool. Otherwise pool exhaustion blocks every incoming request.

questions.question: How does a Canary release differ from a standard Blue-Green deployment?
options: Canary deploys code without automated tests

Blue-Green switches 100% of traffic atomically between two identical environments, whereas Canary routes a small subset (e.g., 5%) of live traffic to the new version first to validate metrics before full rollout
Blue-Green only works for SQL databases
Canary requires shutting down production servers during rollout
questions.explanation: Blue-Green maintains two full environments and flips the router all at once; Canary progressively shifts small traffic percentages while monitoring error/latency SLOs.

questions.question: How is `java.util.HashSet<E>` implemented internally in the JDK?
options: As a sorted Red-Black tree of `E`
Backed by a `HashMap<E, Object>` where elements are keys mapped to a shared dummy constant `PRESENT`
As a bloom filter with fixed 64-bit buckets
questions.explanation: `HashSet` delegates `add/remove/contains` to an internal `HashMap<E, Object>` storing each element as a key with a single dummy `Object PRESENT` value.

questions.question: In SQL, what does the pattern `WHERE code LIKE 'A_B%'` match?
options: Any string starting with `'A'`, followed by ANY single character, then `'B'`, then zero or more characters
Strings containing `'A'`, zero or more chars, then `'B'`
questions.explanation: In SQL `LIKE`, `_` matches any single character and `%` matches zero or more characters.

questions.question: On Unix/Linux, what is a Zombie (`Z` state) process?
options: A process whose parent exited while it is still running
A terminated child process whose exit status has not yet been reaped by its parent via `wait()`/`waitpid()`
A kernel thread executing infinite CPU loops
A swapped-out process waiting for disk I/O
questions.explanation: When a child terminates, its memory is freed, but its process table slot (PID + exit status) remains as a Zombie until the parent calls `wait()`. (An Orphan is a still-running child whose parent died, adopted by `init`/PID 1.)

questions.question: When a browser sends `If-None-Match: "v42"` and the server confirms the resource ETag is still `"v42"`, which HTTP status code should the server return without re-sending the body?
questions.explanation: `304 Not Modified` instructs the client to reuse its cached copy, saving payload bandwidth.

questions.question: Which traversal of a valid Binary Search Tree yields all node keys in non-decreasing sorted order?
questions.explanation: Because every key in the left subtree is <= root <= right subtree, Inorder traversal visits keys in sorted order.

questions.question: What distinguishes the G1 (Garbage-First) collector (default since Java 9) from the older Parallel GC?
options: G1 partitions the heap into equal-sized regions and prioritizes collecting regions with the most garbage first to meet configurable pause-time goals
G1 disables reference counting in Metaspace
questions.explanation: G1 divides the heap into small regions (young/old/humongous) and runs concurrent marking + incremental evacuations prioritizing highest-garbage regions (`Garbage-First`).
